title: Algebraic relative dualizing homothety over arbitrary rings
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of arbitrary commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$, $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$, and give $A$ its $B$-module structure via multiplication. Use the module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived scalar extension and diagonal object [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data], and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. For $T\in D(A)$ put $T_1=T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B$. Say $T$ is $R$-perfect if it is pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and has finite Tor amplitude over $R$: there are integers $a\le b$ with $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for all $R$-modules $Q$ and $i\notin[a,b]$. If $M\in D(A)$ is $R$-perfect and $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,M_1)\cong A[0]$ in $D(B)$, the scalar-action map $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,M)$ (the transpose of the unit action) is an isomorphism in $D(A)$. Consequently scalar multiplication identifies $A$ with $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(M)$ as a ring, identifies $A^\times$ with $\operatorname{Aut}_{D(A)}(M)$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(M,M[i])=0$ for every $i<0$. No Noetherian or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-subring-model-system] to $R\to A$, then start at its flat stage. Obtain a small directed tail of finitely generated integer subalgebras $R_i\subset R$, a flat finitely presented $R_0\to A_0$, and $A_i=A_0\otimes_{R_0}R_i$, $A=A_0\otimes_{R_0}R$. The identifications are compatible with all transition maps. The integers are a PID: in a nonzero ideal choose its least positive integer and use division with remainder to show it generates the ideal; the zero ideal is principal as well. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes $\mathbf Z$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes every $R_i$ and $A_i$ Noetherian. No injectivity of $A_i\to A$ is claimed.

proof.text: Choose a polynomial presentation $P_0=R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A_0$ (finite presentation includes finite generation), and put $C_0=R\operatorname{Hom}_{P_0}(A_0,P_0)[n]$ with the coinduction action. By [lem-trf-algebraic-diagonal-class-normalization], $C_0$ is $R_0$-perfect and $R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_0\otimes_{R_0}A_0}(A_0,(C_0)_1)\cong A_0$. On the one-object ringed site sections are the identity exact functor, so [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] identifies degree zero of this isomorphism with the diagonal Hom module. Choose the inverse image $\gamma_0$ of $1$ under an $A_0$-linear identification of that module with $A_0$. It generates the diagonal Hom module. For every $i$ and also over $R$, apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-diagonal-generator-base-change] to $C_0,\gamma_0$. With $C_i=C_0\otimes_{A_0}^{\mathbf L}A_i$ and $C=C_0\otimes_{A_0}^{\mathbf L}A$, it gives the diagonal-Hom condition and generators $\gamma_i,\gamma$. The maps $R_0\to R_i$ and $R_0\to R$ need not be flat.

source.place: Tag 0E2G, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, proof; Noetherian reduction and filtered continuity. Consequences by scalar action and shifted Hom.

proof.text: The objects $C_i$ and $C$ are relatively perfect. Here is the full translation needed to apply the existing scheme base-change theorem. Under [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] let $E_0=\widetilde C_0$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$. It is pseudo-coherent by [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] and has locally finite Tor dimension over $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ by [lem-trf-affine-relative-tor-amplitude-criterion]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-relative-perfect-base-change] along $\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ and along $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$: the original structure morphism is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], and locally finitely presented by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], using the given global affine presentation as the neighbourhood at every point. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the fibre products are $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with first projection induced by $A_0\to A_i$, $A_0\to A$; then by [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] the outputs are $\widetilde C_i$ and $\widetilde C$. Applying the same two affine criteria in reverse gives pseudo-coherence and finite base-ring Tor amplitude for each. In particular no global amplitude bound for a non-quasi-compact scheme is being inferred. Each scheme here is affine, precisely the hypothesis of the Tor criterion.

source.place: Tag 0E2G, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, proof; Noetherian reduction and filtered continuity. Consequences by scalar action and shifted Hom.

proof.text: Over each Noetherian pair $R_i\to A_i$, the generator $\gamma_i$ from step 2 makes multiplication $A_i\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_i\otimes_{R_i}A_i}(A_i,(C_i)_1)$ an isomorphism: the target has only degree-zero cohomology, freely generated by $\gamma_i$, so that map is an isomorphism on every cohomology group. The derived-category localization at quasi-isomorphisms gives the asserted isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-diagonal-class-normalization] with $M=N=C_i$ and $\gamma=\theta=\gamma_i$. Its hypotheses are step 3 and the preceding multiplication isomorphism. Its conclusion gives the actual scalar map $h_i:A_i\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_i}(C_i,C_i)$ as an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E2G, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, proof; Noetherian reduction and filtered continuity. Consequences by scalar action and shifted Hom.

proof.text:
Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-perfect-hom-filtered-colimit] with $K_0=C_0$, $L_0=C_0[q]$: $C_0$ is pseudo-coherent and its finite $R_0$-Tor interval shifts by $-q$. It gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(C,C[q])=\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_i)}(C_i,C_i[q]).$$
By [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and the shift convention of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], the groups on the right are $H^qR\operatorname{Hom}_{A_i}(C_i,C_i)$, hence are $A_i$ for $q=0$ and zero otherwise, by step 4. These identifications respect the transition maps: derived extension takes $a\,1_{C_i}$ to its image scalar times $1_{C_j}$, since tensoring sends $a(z)\otimes t$ to $z\otimes at$. Thus the degree-zero map is exactly $a\mapsto a\,1_C$ and identifies the colimit with $A$; for $q\ne0$ the groups vanish. The same Hom/cohomology identification shows that the actual transpose $h_C:A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$ is an isomorphism on every cohomology group, so is an isomorphism in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This does not assert arbitrary base change of the whole unbounded Hom complex.

source.place: Tag 0E2G, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, proof; Noetherian reduction and filtered continuity. Consequences by scalar action and shifted Hom.

proof.text: Both $C$ and the supplied $M$ are $R$-perfect and satisfy the diagonal-Hom condition, by steps 2--3 and the hypotheses. Therefore [lem-sfb-arbitrary-ring-relative-dualizing-isomorphism] gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. Conjugation gives an isomorphism $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,M)\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$ by the two-variable functor [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. It sends $h_M$ to $h_C$: for any scalar $a$, $u(a m)=a u(m)$, and equivalently the transposes agree by the naturality of the unit action. Thus $h_M$ is an isomorphism. No preservation of the chosen diagonal generator by $u$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0E2G, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, proof; Noetherian reduction and filtered continuity. Consequences by scalar action and shifted Hom.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and the Hom shift formula of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(M,M[q])\cong H^qR\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,M)$. The isomorphism $h_M$ identifies these with $H^q(A[0])$. For $q<0$ this is zero. For $q=0$ the resulting bijection is scalar multiplication $A\to\operatorname{End}(M)$; it preserves sums, products and $1$ since $(a\,1_M)(b\,1_M)=ab\,1_M$. Its units are precisely the invertible endomorphisms, so it also identifies $A^\times$ with $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$. If $A=0$, the derived category has only its zero object; these assertions include its one-element endomorphism ring and automorphism group.
